# Angular

**21.2, standalone components**, in exactly one place: the lab 4 SPA of
[[information-systems-modelling]]. It is the only Angular in the source set — every other frontend in
the corpus is either [[react]] or hand-written vanilla JS.

## The stack as pinned

`dependencies`: `@angular/{common,compiler,core,forms,platform-browser,platform-server,router}` ^21.2,
**`@angular/ssr` ^21.2.7**, `express` ^5.1.0, `rxjs` ~7.8, `tslib`.
`devDependencies`: `@angular/build`, `@angular/cli`, `@angular/compiler-cli`, `@types/express`,
`@types/node`, `jsdom`, **`json-server`**, `prettier` ^3.8.1, `typescript` ~5.9.2, **`vitest` ^4.0.8**.
`packageManager: npm@11.11.0`.

Three of those are worth stopping on.

**`vitest`, not Karma/Jasmine.** The Angular default test runner is absent; `jsdom` plus vitest 4
replaces it. This matches the corpus habit of preferring the lighter runner, but it is the only
Angular project available to compare against.

**`@angular/ssr` + express in an SPA.** The app is documented as a browser client talking to Spring
Boot on port 8080, and server-side rendering is lab **6's** stated topic, not lab 4's. The
`serve:ssr:*` script exists and the server entry point is generated.

**`json-server` as a devDependency.** A leftover from the pre-rewrite scaffold below; nothing in the
live app uses it.

## Two Angular apps, one directory inside the other

`lab4/angular-rest-client-student-crud/` is the real ModellingClub SPA — components and feature
routing, a REST client against the Spring API, views guarded on the presence of a JWT (see
[[stateless-jwt-authentication]]).

Nested **inside** it sits `angular-rest-client-student-crud/angular-rest-client-student-crud/` — a
39-file copy of the original assignment's *student* CRUD scaffold, complete with its own `db.json`
for `json-server`. It is dead: nothing imports it, nothing builds it. It survives as one of four
instances of [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] in this repo.

⚠ The nested duplicate is also where all the `.spec.ts` files live. **The live SPA has one
`app.spec.ts` and no feature tests** — so the test files a reader finds by globbing belong to the
dead app.

## Why Angular at all

Not a free choice: lab 1's own requirements document proposes a Linux / Python / PostgreSQL / Nginx
stack, and the labs answer the same requirements on Java + Angular instead. That is recorded as
[[java-angular-over-the-specs-python-stack]] — the requirements are treated as the contract and the
technology as a choice, stated in those words in the root README.
